title: "Tags"
description: "Mark items as vegetarian, spicy, new, or chef's pick. Diners see them on every dish, and the assistant reads them."
sidebarTitle: "Tags"
icon: "tag"
---

Tags are short labels you attach to menu items — *Vegetarian*, *Spicy*,
*Chef's pick*. Diners see them as coloured pills next to each dish, and the
menu assistant reads them when someone asks *"what's vegetarian here?"*.

## Platform presets vs your custom tags

Rumizi ships a set of curated presets — the common ones like *Vegetarian*,
*Vegan*, *Spicy*, *Gluten-free*, *New*, *Chef's pick*. These come with
consistent translations across every supported language.

You can also create **custom tags** that only exist for your venue. For
example, *"Nonna's recipe"* or *"House special"*.

<Note>
Adopting a platform preset takes a **snapshot** into your venue. If the
preset text changes later on the platform, your adopted copy doesn't
change — you keep what you picked.
</Note>

## Adding a tag to an item

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the item">
    In the menu editor **Items** tab, tap the item you want to tag.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Open the tag picker">
    Tap the tag area. You'll see your existing tags plus the platform
    presets you haven't adopted yet.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick or create">
    Tap an existing tag to apply it, or tap **New tag** to create a
    custom one with your own label and colour.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save the item">
    The tag appears on the item card and, once you publish, on the diner's
    menu.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Where to manage them

Tags have their own **Tags** tab in the menu editor — that's where you
create them, rename them, adopt presets, and set colours and icons. You can
also apply an existing tag from inside the item dialog on the **Items** tab
while you're editing a dish.

## What diners see

Tags show up as small coloured labels:

- **On item cards** in the menu — the first three, then a "+2" for the
  rest.
- **On the item detail page** — all of them.

<Note>
Tags are **labels, not filters**. There's no filter bar on the public menu
today: diners narrow things down with the search box (which matches names,
descriptions, ingredients, and allergens) or by asking the
[menu assistant](/diners/menu-assistant) — *"which of these are
vegetarian?"* — which reads your tags and answers from them.
</Note>

## Custom colours and icons

Each tag can have its own colour and an optional icon. Pick colours that
are readable on both light and dark backgrounds — the menu theme colours
show through.
